account:
Today has seemed quiet from what I have personally seen and heard. I kept my market walk, town accounts, dockside tea, and afternoon office appointments. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. The secretary says no correspondence or other official business has arrived.

The only complication was identifying my tea host: the appointment book gave merely a neighbour at an east-bank dockside cottage, and the secretary's inquiries did not establish which one. I found the neighbour at the cottage near road point (16, -60, 105), kept our tea appointment, and have now given the secretary that location for tomorrow. The neighbour reported no pressing concerns and spoke pleasantly about visiting the bakery and meeting people.

Several townsfolk earlier said the baker was carrying wheat at the bakery; the neighbour said the baker was busy preparing fresh market loaves. I later saw the builder walking near the town hall carrying a lantern and a sack of bread. I do not know why the builder had that quantity of bread, and have no evidence that it is connected to any problem.

The secretary has returned the appointment book to its chest and is helping prepare tomorrow's ten o'clock mill grain inspection. I requested existing stock and delivery records and information about shortages or storage concerns, without moving supplies. This is routine preparation, not a response to any shortage I have verified. I remain at the town hall and should return home for my nineteen o'clock appointment.
